clue.text: Tax one no longer has to pay Gordon Brown, e.g.

definitions.text: Tax one no longer has to pay
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old local levy
second meaning: a person from Scotland, as the former British prime minister is

explanation.surface: A grumble about some levy a former Chancellor and Prime Minister no longer has to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a British Chancellor and Prime Minister, so the clue reads as tax politics; he is simply an example of a man from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic municipal tax called scot is obsolete, and Gordon Brown is a native of Scotland, an example of the nationality.

clue.text: Covering vehicle with plastic

parts.note: an everyday vehicle
PET is polyethylene terephthalate, the plastic of drinks bottles

explanation.surface: A car seat or interior lined with plastic sheeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a floor covering, so the noun covering names it by its function.

clue.text: Revelation of a short ballad penned by formidable storyteller

indicators.note: what is penned by someone is written inside their pen, enclosed by their name

parts.note: taken as written
Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales of horror

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the ballad drops its last letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean ballad, here trimmed of its final O

explanation.surface: A disclosure in some brief ballad written by a terrifying teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed calypso sits inside Poe, after the opening A. Revelation is also the Bible book called the Apocalypse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation is also known as the Apocalypse, and the word originally means an uncovering or disclosure.

clue.text: Sanctuary of some uneasy luminaries

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying across two words

parts.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Nervous celebrities seeking a safe refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection granted to a refugee, the same idea as sanctuary given in a church.

clue.text: Historiographer; a new name on American database

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for new
standard abbreviation for name
standard abbreviation for American
a list is a simple store of records

explanation.surface: A historian has their name newly added to a US database.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the database after the abbreviations, as in a down clue one piece sits on another.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year records of events, which makes them a chronicler of history.

clue.text: Malay chief somewhat open about …

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door ajar is slightly open

explanation.surface: A Malay ruler who is fairly frank, with the clue running into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the following clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Raja is the title of a ruler or prince in Malaysia and India, so it names a Malay chief.

clue.text: … most turbulent period of activity including wisecrack occasionally

indicators.note: a word including something holds it within its own letters

parts.note: a fest is a festival or spell of busy celebration

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word counts

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The wildest stretch of busy times, with the odd quip thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue; only 'most turbulent' defines here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce weather or fighting is wild and violent, so the superlative means most turbulent.

clue.text: Anytime, lad performing in a spirited way

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new routine

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy ready to go on stage at any moment, full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something animatedly means doing it with liveliness and vigour, a synonym of spiritedly.

clue.text: Crush successful combatant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to munch or chew noisily, as a horse does its bit
second meaning: short for champion, a winner

explanation.surface: Flatten the fighter who has won.
explanation.walkthrough: Crush looks like defeating an opponent, but it is the verb for chewing hard; the noun is a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to munch or mash, and the noun is the informal clipping of champion, a winning fighter.

clue.text: Sorted out tensions surrounding a matter of excited public interest

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the word's letters are rearranged
surrounding means placed all round something else, enclosing it

parts.note: rearranged letters of the word, to be split around the article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calming strained relations over a matter the public is buzzing about.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is an event that causes widespread excitement and interest, such as a news story.

clue.text: Very hot and humid, lacking river current

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: the climate of the tropics
standard abbreviation for river, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Sultry weather where there's no flow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River current' reads as one phrase; current is detached as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means of present interest, dealing with current affairs, so it fits current as an adjective.

clue.text: A ragman, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters given are only one arrangement of many

parts.note: the seven letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and definition at once: the phrase is a rearrangement of the answer, and the answer is what the phrase is.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words use exactly the letters of the solution, so the phrase is an example of a rearranged word.

clue.text: Like some elements of dinner, say, including starter of tapas

definitions.note: adjectival: metal used as a modifier, as in metal elements

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

indicators.note: 'starter of' keeps only the first letter of 'tapas'

parts.note: the opening letter of tapas

explanation.surface: Describing parts of a Spanish dinner that begins with small dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements of dinner' reads as courses, but elements are chemical ones such as iron and copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Most chemical elements, iron, copper and gold among them, are classed as metals.

clue.text: Music producer's complaint about composer spending a grand

indicators.note: about means around, so the complaint wraps round what follows

parts.note: a moan is a grumble

indicators.note: spending means paying out, so the composer gives up a letter

parts.note: an author composes words; the A is spent
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A record producer grumbles about a songwriter who blew a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a studio boss but means an instrument; 'composer' is a writer of words, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica produces music when blown, so it is literally a producer of music.

clue.text: Undisciplined he-man ties sailor's rope

indicators.note: undisciplined means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild macho type knots the rope on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: On a yacht the mainsheet is the line that controls the angle of the mainsail, a rope a sailor handles.

clue.text: Whales turning up on beach, mostly caught over time, must not be injured

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: orcas are killer whales

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of; the D is dropped
cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
T for time, after the rest

explanation.surface: Whales stranded on a beach, nearly trapped by the tide, must be kept from harm.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scoring, where it marks a batsman out by a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred to be violated or harmed, hence it must not be injured.

clue.text: Outdistance ship at sea that's not taking Polish on board

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Outrunning a vessel at sea that is not carrying Poles aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish at the start of a word disguises the lower-case sense of refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has not absorbed polish, meaning refinement, lacks worldly sophistication.

clue.text: Lover's song composed, welcoming publicity

indicators.note: welcoming means letting someone in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: composed means calm and untroubled
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A love song was written and then promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Composed looks like the act of writing the song, but it is the adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song sung by a lover beneath the beloved's window at night.

clue.text: Well-organised isle ends reluctance to work

indicators.note: something well organised has been put into good order, here a new order of letters

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy island puts a stop to people shirking.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is laziness, an unwillingness to do any work.

clue.text: Peter Shaffer's Equus maybe? Rough stuff!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a stage drama about horses

explanation.walkthrough: Equus is a play by Peter Shaffer about a boy who blinds horses, so it is a horse play; the answer as one word is rough-and-tumble fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous, rough-and-tumble behaviour is called horseplay, while a drama about horses is literally a play about horses.

clue.text: When upset, concerning male might whine

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down entry the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning
standard abbreviation for male
may and might both express possibility

explanation.surface: A man who is upset about something may well complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain or chatter in a loud, persistent, whining voice.

clue.text: Before change occurs, duck egg's released from here

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O
vary means alter

explanation.surface: A duck egg hatches, or is laid, just before a change happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the duck in front of the change. 'Duck egg' reads together, but duck is the cricket zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The ovary is the female organ that produces and releases eggs, so it is where an egg comes from.

clue.text: Attraction of every Yorkshire river

parts.note: all and every both mean the whole number
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The charm of each river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure, a river in northern England, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is the quality of being powerfully attractive or enticing, a synonym of attraction.

clue.text: Speak disparagingly to derelict

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to criticise or belittle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests insulting a vagrant; the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to belittle them, and a run-down building is shabby and neglected.

clue.text: Comply with old Ottoman ruler

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: Follow the orders of a former Turkish governor.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey a rule or order is to comply with it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Assuming student free from pain after dose of medicine ultimately cures illness

indicators.note: a dose is a small measure, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: assuming means taking on or adopting, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to ease is to relieve pain
L for learner, from the plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A learner relieved of pain once a course of medicine cures the disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the eased learner after the M. L comes from the L-plate on a learner driver's car in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is an infectious viral disease marked by a red rash, so it is an illness.

clue.text: Beer knocked over in error

indicators.note: a thing knocked over is upended, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: pils is short for Pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A drink spilt by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, as in a slip of the tongue, so it means an error.

clue.text: Say further with resolution and observe intended recipient

parts.note: to add is to say more
res is an abbreviation for resolution
see and observe are synonyms

explanation.surface: Speak on with determination and watch who the message is meant for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the pieces; resolution looks like determination but stands for its abbreviation, as in screen resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The addressee is the person to whom a letter or remark is directed, the recipient it was meant for.

clue.text: Measure US soldier's pet?

parts.note: a cor is a Hebrew measure of capacity
GI is an American infantryman

explanation.surface: Sizing up an American soldier's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example; the cor is an obscure Biblical measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh dog breed kept as a companion animal, an example of a pet.
